context.process_name: Subsequent Closes: Equalization Interest & Investor Rebalance
context.objective: Document how we carry out Subsequent Closes: Equalization Interest & Investor Rebalance, the controls and what needs confirmation.

turns.text: Oh, it kicks off when someone comes into the fund late, or an investor bumps up their commitment, that kind of thing. It just happens whenever, not on a schedule.
How do you learn that an investor has joined late or increased their commitment?
The client sends a close notification, and there is the signed subscription or commitment increase paperwork that comes with it.
Once you receive the close notification and signed paperwork, what do you do first?
Someone on the team opens up the close and does the usual checks to make sure it is ready to go, writes down the basics and stuff.
What are they checking to decide the close is ready to go?

The fund admin preparer confirms the client approved the admission, AML is cleared, and the system and portal onboarding is done. If documents are incomplete or the AML, commitment or effective date records are missing, it gets escalated and no equalization call goes out for that investor.
Once those prerequisites are cleared, what does the preparer do next?
Then they sort out which rules apply, the agreement stuff, with the reviewer and the client or legal chiming in. It gets written up and locked.
How do the applicable agreement terms determine the equalization interest and investor rebalance?

The partnership agreement and side letters set the rate, the start and end dates, day count, compounding and who gets the interest, plus which earlier calls count. We never assume any of that, and if it is unclear the work pauses until the client or legal gives written direction.
Once the applicable terms are written up and locked, how do you calculate the equalization interest and investor rebalance?

Well, first the preparer pulls together the list of all the earlier capital calls and ties it out, and the reviewer verifies it. Then they work out what the new investor would have put in on each call, and the interest goes on top of that per the agreement.
What does the reviewer compare to verify the earlier capital-call tie-out?

memo_findings.answer: Subsequent Closes: Equalization Interest & Investor Rebalance

The work kicks off when an investor enters the fund late or an investor increases their commitment. The participant reports that it happens whenever such an event occurs, not on a schedule.
Who receives the client's close notification and accompanying signed subscription or commitment-increase paperwork remains unknown.

A team member opens the close, performs readiness checks and writes down the basics.
The fund admin preparer confirms admission approval, AML clearance and completed system and portal onboarding. If documents are incomplete or AML, commitment or effective-date records are missing, the issue is escalated and no equalization call goes out for that investor.
After prerequisites are cleared, the preparer sorts out which agreement rules apply with input from the reviewer and the client or legal. The determination is written up and locked.
If applicable agreement terms are unclear, the work pauses until the client or legal gives written direction; the team does not assume the terms.
After the applicable terms are written up and locked, the preparer assembles and ties out a list of all earlier capital calls; the reviewer verifies it. The preparer then works out what the new investor would have contributed on each call and adds interest under the agreement.

The fund admin preparer confirms client approval of the admission, AML clearance, and completion of system and portal onboarding.
The escalation recipient, resolution and return-to-work path for incomplete documents or missing records remain unspecified.
Incomplete documents or missing AML, commitment or effective-date records are escalated, and no equalization call goes out for the affected investor.
The preparer ties out the list of earlier capital calls, and the reviewer verifies it before the per-call investor amounts are worked out.
The sources and comparison used to tie out the earlier-call list, and what the reviewer verifies, remain unspecified.

No equalization call goes out for an investor when documents are incomplete or AML, commitment or effective-date records are missing; the issue is escalated.

The partnership agreement and side letters set the interest rate, start and end dates, day count, compounding, interest recipients and which earlier calls count.
The team does not assume agreement terms; unclear terms require written direction from the client or legal before work continues.
For each earlier call, the preparer works out what the new investor would have contributed, with interest added according to the agreement.

open_questions: Who receives the client notification, and are there fixed deadlines for this event-driven work?
Who is accountable for the overall result, and what shows the process is complete?
Who receives readiness escalations, how are issues resolved, and where does the work resume? What happens when another prerequisite fails?
Who interprets and locks the terms, where is the interpretation recorded, and how does work resume after written direction?
What does the preparer tie the earlier-call list to, what does the reviewer verify, and what happens if the check fails?
Who performs the calculations, where are they recorded, and how are commitment increases handled?
How are interest and the investor rebalance calculated, checked, approved and delivered after the per-call amounts are worked out?
What evidence is retained, where, and what system is authoritative for the material results?
Is this general GPFS practice or client-specific, and what is the basis for that assessment? What variations and charging or removal constraints apply?
What downstream process uses the output, and what dependencies must be complete before delivery?
What are the main exceptions, manual difficulties, risks, volumes and effort? Are there procedures or examples available for review?
